interpretation.positive: Reusing the existing exhaustive spatial cohort increases Japanese primary-trait coverage beyond the balanced Chapter 1 atlas without any new biological sampling.
interpretation.limitation: Coverage is still too sparse for a radiation-wide Japanese trait-rate claim: only six distinct Japan-38 trait taxa have at least ten strict spatial observations, and broad C. japonicum / C. nipponicum image concepts cannot be silently assigned to paper varieties.
interpretation.next_action: Use the exhaustive cohort as the first primary-trait recovery layer, then target the remaining Japan-38 trait gaps with existing public images/herbarium evidence before field collection. Auxiliary involucre/spine proxies remain limited to the high-resolution Chapter 1 layer unless separately re-extracted.

claim_boundary: This is a trait-coverage audit, not an evolutionary-rate result. Observation counts do not establish independent populations, genetic variation, taxon-concept identity, adaptation or ancestral state.
